name: prov_annotate
description: Add moirai provenance to an application - find data accesses, agree entity types and activities with the user, insert them into a copy (decorate a function, patch or subclass a method, annotate a statement, record a shell step of a Maestro YAML, invalidate, conditional edges), validate, and show the user an entity-type relationship diagram of what was annotated at the gate. Load for the annotate stage, or when a spec needs an inherited method, an inline subprocess step, a delete, a key from a local variable or an optional input, when the work is a shell command in a Maestro YAML `cmd:` step (AlphaFold 3, Rosetta FlexPepDock, BioTox, yaml_step), when a question about the parameters or flags of a step finds none recorded (a no-argument on_finish/run/__call__ hook whose command line was built in the constructor), when a gap says no_outputs or no_attributes (a hook that returns None keeps its result on self: record it with capture.outputs and as attributes; a question about quality, depth, size or counts of a data entity finds no attributes), or when the annotate verdict is inconclusive about PYTHONPATH, moirai_env.sh or maestro_dry.

history.why: Elmerfold annotate (pipeline elmerfold-prov-20261030-125944) could not express: the driver->server inference_request hop (ServerTask.start), inline subprocess steps (template_hits was 'generated by no activity'), deletes (moirai has INVALIDATED), ids from statement-level locals, conditional used edges for allow_failure outputs, an input_chunk->sequence entity edge, and an unchecked _moirai_prov.py PYTHONPATH rule. Adds spec fields mode patch|subclass|statement, invalidated, updated, when, relations; an offline annotate_preview that runs the annotated code against a fake moirai; and validator checks names_resolve, helper_single, helper_on_pythonpath. Existing specs generate byte-identical code.

Process feedback fb-3422517747 (pipeline elmerfold-prov-20261030-125944, annotate gate): show the user an entity-type relationship diagram of what was annotated, as the high-level view they decide from. Adds annotate_diagram (pipeline; writes provenance/annotation_diagram.md and returns the Mermaid text, counts computed from the applied spec, size-budget collapse reported) and annotate_diagram_preview (same on a spec, no pipeline). Tool-design fault: annotate_validate left helper_on_pythonpath as unknown until integrate wrote moirai_env.sh, but integrate comes after annotate, so the verdict was inconclusive and pipeline_advance refused forever. A check owned by a later stage is now a deferred note (key deferred, with the owning stage), not counted in the verdict; enforcement moves to moirai_integrate's validator (separate proposal). Adds annotate_validate_preview to reproduce it offline.

BioTox annotate (pipeline biotox-prov-20261030-134517): AlphaFold 3 and Rosetta run as shell commands inside Maestro YAML `cmd: |` steps, which annotate_apply could not hook (Python functions/statements and C/C++ functions only). af3_msa, af3_infer, peptide_prepack and peptide_docking had no provenance, predicted_complex and docking_scores were downgraded from scientific artifacts to intermediates (annotate_spec rejects an artifact no activity generates), msa_input and prediction_ranking were dropped, and joins broke at cut_complex and docking_scores. Adds mode yaml_step: a text-level wrapper inserted at the top of a step's cmd block (comments and layout of the YAML are untouched) that installs an EXIT trap; when the step ends it calls the single root _moirai_prov.py as a script (python found from MOIRAI_PYTHON, MOIRAI_SERVICE or moirai-service on PATH, resolved before the step activates its own venv, run with PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME/LD_PRELOAD unset) with used/generated rows whose files exist. It runs in a subshell with its output discarded, never calls exit, so the step's exit status and early `exit 0`/`exit 1` flow are unchanged, and a missing or broken moirai is skipped. Keys are Maestro-substituted text, so both sides of a hop get the same type and key. annotate_spec accepts artifacts generated only by yaml_step activities. annotate_validate adds yaml_intact (stripping the wrapper gives back the source byte for byte), bash_syntax, maestro_dry (maestro run --dry on source and on copy; inconclusive when the source cannot be dry-run either) and names_resolve for $(VAR), $(step.workspace) and shell variables. annotate_preview can run the wrapped steps against a fake moirai. Existing specs generate byte-identical code.

Defect (annotate_validate 19/20 twice in pipeline biotox-prov-big-20261104-124916): _maestro_dry ran `maestro run --dry` on a temp copy of the annotated tree without the tree on PYTHONPATH. The annotated BioTox gen.py starts with `import _moirai_prov` (helper at the tree root); Maestro loads the parameter generator by file path, so the import raised ImportError, Maestro fell back to `import imp` and died with ModuleNotFoundError on Python 3.12, and maestro_dry:biotox.yaml wrongly failed ('the wrapper broke the YAML'). Fix: the dry-run env now has PYTHONPATH = <temp copy of the tree> + os.pathsep + existing PYTHONPATH (HOME stays the temp dir); the real tree is untouched; the source-tree dry run gets the same harmless prepend. New check reproduces it with /bin/sh as a fake maestro that runs a file `run` from the tree (cwd) and fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'imp' when _moirai_prov.py is in the cwd but PYTHONPATH lacks the tree; before the fix the verdict is fail, after it pass. Built on active version 4.

Built on ACTIVE v5. Measured diagnosis (session biotox/20261104_204918, scratch /tmp/haridev/dry2): maestro run --dry of the annotated BioTox YAML fails with PYTHONPATH none (ModuleNotFoundError _moirai_prov, masked by No module named 'imp' from maestrowf/maestro.py:351) and with the tree only (what v5 sets; _moirai_prov.py:8 import moirai -> No module named 'moirai', moirai is not in biotox-env), and passes (rc 0, 10 combinations) with exactly what moirai_env.sh exports: <provenance>/moirai_shim:<tree copy>. Change: (1) _maestro_dry takes env_file and swap; its PYTHONPATH is the export PYTHONPATH value of work/moirai_env.sh with the annotated root replaced by the temp tree copy and the trailing ${PYTHONPATH...} expansion dropped, prepended to os.environ PYTHONPATH; no file or no PYTHONPATH line: only the tree copy. (2) when the tail has No module named 'imp', the first earlier exception of the output is reported (first error: ...). (3) checks: v5 check kept, new check with a fake maestro that needs a shim dir holding a moirai entry AND the tree on PYTHONPATH (fails with old code), new check for the masked-cause report.

Capture context, so questions like 'what are the filter parameters' can be answered: every activity records what it was run with (<activity>.inputs, role parameter, used: its arguments with defaults, the attributes of the object it runs on, the flags of any command line among them, and capture.inputs expressions; for a Maestro step the $(VAR) study variables its command uses) and what it returned (<activity>.output, generated); entities may name attributes (an <type>.attributes entity part_of it). Values are compact JSON in the uri ('json:{...}'). Entity type descriptions list attributes and the expected producing and using activities. Capturing never raises into the application.

Capture context, so questions like 'what are the filter parameters' can be answered: every activity records what it was run with - one <activity>.input entity (role parameter, used) per value, uri name=value: its arguments with defaults, the attributes of the object it runs on, the flags of every command line among them (flags first), capture.inputs expressions; for a Maestro step the $(VAR) study variables its command uses - and what it returned (<activity>.output, generated); entities may name attributes (<type>.attribute entities, part_of it). One entity per value because a trace keeps ~250 characters of a uri and rewrites quotes and brackets. Entity type descriptions list attributes and the expected producing and using activities. Capturing never raises into the application.

Gap G-082a03t0 (pipeline elmerfold-prov-20261030-125944): a no-argument hook method (on_finish(self)) of an object whose command line was built in its constructor and stored on self recorded no parameters; the annotation had no capture. Rule, exploration steps and a reproducing annotate_preview case added to the skill. Skill text only; tool and existing checks unchanged.

Gaps G-71ce0cb0 (no_outputs, missed_outputs) and G-9e3bd857 (no_attributes, missed_attributes) from the question about the quality and depth of the MSAs: a hook returning None keeps its result on self, so default output capture recorded nothing; entities read through an index carried no attributes. Skill-only: new rules, corrector rows for no_outputs and no_attributes.

Gap G-71ce0cb0 (no_outputs, activity filter_msa) kept coming back: an attributes-only fix on the generated entity does not feed the {op: outputs, activity} query, which reads the activity's <activity>.output entities, and those could only come from a return value. The hook MMseqsFilterTask.on_finish(self) returns None and its result lives on self.stdout. Adds capture.outputs: {label: expression}, evaluated after the call over the arguments, self and result (statement: its locals), guarded, one <activity>.output entity (generated, name=value) per label, in addition to the return value. Updated: helper (_emit_outputs, _output, _outputs, activity, event), spec emitter _kw, _exprs scope validation (names_resolve), _check_spec, annotate_spec docstring, SKILL.md; two preview checks added.

User: "can u support quality of msas". Answer said traces give depth but not quality (no coverage, identity or e-value). Add a generic rule: quality is a set of cheap computed metrics recorded as attributes, placed on a worker activity, with the stated limits of the data.

Gap G-450f0964 (no_inputs on statement activity load_inputs, pipeline elmerfold-prov-20261030-125944, answer 3d170edb64): a statement activity has no automatic input capture, so it recorded no .input entities; the rule, explore checklist item and Corrector row were missing.

Generic lessons from a 23-gap batch on the Elmerfold app; user: 'Improve the provenance coverage for all 23 open gaps'. Adds a section on relating an entity in every activity, subprocess failures, environment facts, how-many/which-one values, and reading annotate_apply unresolved.

The user asked for the four aspects of provenance (traceability, accountability, decision making, performance), each its own capability, and for one reading capability (prov_read: TraceViewer) used by every graph, query and check. The helper records a run_context entity at start (user, group, command and working dir only as hashes; the names as identity entities related to nothing, dropped to anonymize; job, host, versions) and passes the hashes to moirai.metadata when moirai has it.

moirai now records user_hash, group_hash, job and the configuration environment as process metadata at initialize (branch feat/process-metadata); the helper's run_context uses moirai's identity hash (moirai_hash of kind and MOIRAI_ID_SALT + name) so both name a user the same way.

User: "I want to add the perf annotation as a part of annotation sub capability for performance provenance it should add dftracer calls directly for performance apis." Stage 1 placeholder: a `performance` spec section applied by annotate_apply in the same pass (core/perf_annotate.py), validated by annotate_validate and drawn in annotate_diagram. Full skill, code and checks follow by capability_refine.
